scope: Configuration track only: define the repository-owned desired policy, its exact file layout and schemas, distribution artifacts, GitHub adapters, reconciliation of remote GitHub settings/Projects state, and safe upgrade mechanics across many repositories. It does not make Git the transaction log for live work, replace a durable controller, choose product priority, or let an agent approve changes to permissions, rules, evaluators, or its own policy. The boundary is deliberate: issue forms, workflows and instructions are read directly from a commit, while rulesets, Actions settings, custom properties and GitHub Project fields/items are remote resources and therefore require observed-state inventory and reconciliation [GitHub Projects API: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects; OpenGitOps: https://opengitops.dev/].
current_capabilities: GitHub natively consumes issue forms from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, workflow YAML from `.github/workflows`, `CODEOWNERS`, and repository Copilot instructions. Current Copilot documentation recognizes `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, path-scoped `.github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md`, and nearest-directory `AGENTS.md` precedence [https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions]. These files are declarative inputs at a Git SHA, but GitHub does not validate an organization-specific agent policy schema unless CI does so.

A reusable workflow is a YAML file directly in `.github/workflows` (subdirectories are unsupported) with `on: workflow_call`. A caller uses `owner/repo/.github/workflows/file.yml@ref`; nested chains allow the top caller plus nine reusable levels, loops are forbidden, every workflow must be accessible, and token permissions can only stay the same or decrease down the chain [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows]. Reusable workflows centralize whole jobs; composite actions centralize step sequences [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/create-actions/create-a-composite-action].

An organization `.github` repository can supply workflow templates from `workflow-templates/<name>.yml` plus `<name>.properties.json` and `$default-branch` substitution [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/create-workflow-templates]. It can also supply default community-health files when a repository lacks a local file; on GitHub.com the `.github` repository must be public, so this inheritance mechanism is unsuitable for confidential policy [https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file].

Template repositories bootstrap code: a new repository starts with a single unrelated-history commit and can copy only the default branch or all branches [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-repository-from-a-template]. They are not an upgrade channel: later template changes do not flow to created repositories.

Projects are API-managed through GraphQL, not repository files. `addProjectV2ItemById` and `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` are separate calls; a caller cannot add and update an item in one call [https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects]. Organization-level `projects_v2` and `projects_v2_item` webhooks exist but the current event documentation labels Projects webhooks public preview and subject to change [https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects-v2]. Therefore an event is a reconciliation hint, not proof of complete state.

Repository and organization rulesets are remote policy. Multiple applicable rulesets layer with branch protection; GitHub documents a maximum of 75 repository rulesets and 75 organization-wide rulesets, visible to repository readers, and allows selected roles, teams or GitHub Apps to bypass [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets]. REST/GraphQL can manage organization rulesets [https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-rulesets-for-repositories-in-your-organization]. Repository custom properties provide a centrally queryable inventory/selector for managed repositories [https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-custom-properties-for-repositories-in-your-organization; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/custom-properties].
representative_systems: GitHub-native layer: Issues/issue forms, Projects v2 GraphQL plus organization webhooks, repository/organization rulesets, CODEOWNERS, Actions permissions, reusable workflows, composite actions, workflow templates, template repositories, custom properties, and a GitHub App. These are complementary mechanisms, not one declarative configuration system.

Standards/patterns: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 for machine validation [https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core]; SemVer 2.0.0 for public schema/CLI compatibility promises [https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html]; OpenGitOps for declarative, versioned/immutable, pulled and continuously reconciled desired state [https://opengitops.dev/]; SLSA v1.2 for build/provenance controls on distributed CLI/action artifacts [https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/requirements].

Reusable distribution examples: Renovate shareable presets support centralized configuration via `extends`, while its GitHub Actions manager updates pinned action references [https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-presets/; https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/github-actions/]. OpenSSF Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check and zizmor provide independent static checks for workflow risks [https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies; https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor]. These tools inform the design but do not reconcile GitHub Projects or authorize policy promotion.
primary_evidence: Repository-consumed schema and precedence are documented by GitHub: issue-form syntax [https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema], default health files [https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file], CODEOWNERS [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners], and Copilot/AGENTS instructions [https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/add-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions].

Reuse and bootstrap behavior comes from GitHub's reusable-workflow, sharing, workflow-template and repository-template documentation [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/share-across-private-repositories; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/create-workflow-templates; https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-repository-from-a-template].

Remote-state behavior comes from GitHub's Projects API guide, GraphQL mutation reference, Projects webhook contract, rulesets REST/API documentation, and custom-property APIs [https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects; https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue; https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects-v2; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/rules; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/custom-properties].

Security controls come from GitHub's secure-use and token syntax: pinning a third-party action to a full commit SHA is documented as the only immutable release form; declaring any `permissions` entries sets unspecified permissions to `none`; `pull_request_target` can receive read/write repository permission even for a public fork [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions].
independent_evidence: ARGUS evaluated 2,778,483 workflows referring to 31,725 actions and reported critical code-injection vulnerabilities in 4,307 workflows and 80 actions. This shows that reusable automation increases dependency and injection surface; static linting and restricted contexts are required, and centralization is not itself safety [Muralee et al., USENIX Security 2023: https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity23/presentation/muralee].

The March 2025 `tj-actions/changed-files` compromise affected an action used by more than 23,000 repositories; attackers retroactively moved version tags and the malicious action printed CI/CD secrets to logs. It directly falsifies the claim that a major-version tag is an immutable or sufficiently safe distribution pin [StepSecurity, 2025-03-18: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised; Wiz analysis: https://www.wiz.io/blog/new-github-action-supply-chain-attack-reviewdog-action-setup].

GitHub itself warns that sharing a private action/workflow repository lets outside collaborators in consuming repositories indirectly access it and view run logs; the download token has scoped read access and expires [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/share-across-private-repositories]. This challenges the common assumption that a private central workflow is invisible to every consumer collaborator.

AgentDojo demonstrates prompt-injection attacks against tool-using agents and evaluates defenses [Debenedetti et al., 2024: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352]. Therefore repository text, issues and workflow output are untrusted data; `AGENTS.md` is guidance, not a permission boundary. OWASP's 2025 LLM Top 10 independently identifies prompt injection and excessive agency [https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/assets/PDF/OWASP-Top-10-for-LLMs-v2025.pdf].
metrics_and_limits: Reusable workflows must be directly under `.github/workflows`, and the supported nesting depth is ten total levels; permissions cannot be elevated through a nested chain [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows]. Treat these as platform limits, not recommended architecture; the proposed design permits at most two reusable levels to keep provenance and failures legible.

Rulesets: current GitHub documentation says up to 75 per repository and 75 organization-wide [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets]. Applicable rules layer, so a reconciler must inspect the aggregate policy rather than assume its own named ruleset is the only enforcement source.

GraphQL's general user primary limit is 5,000 points/hour (10,000 in specified Enterprise-owned/approved app cases), with separate secondary limits and node/query constraints [https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api]. Budget inventory calls, paginate, cache IDs only as hints, and back off using response metadata.

Webhook receivers should subscribe only to needed events, validate a secret, answer within 10 seconds, redeliver failures and use `X-GitHub-Delivery` as a delivery identifier [https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks; https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries]. The contract still requires deduplication and periodic full inventory; no completeness or exactly-once guarantee is inferred.

Evidence has no defensible universal number for repositories per controller, upgrade frequency, or reconciliation SLO. Set initial local targets instead: 15-minute full-drift detection for a pilot of 10 repositories; webhook enqueue under 10 seconds; zero destructive automatic changes; 100% SHA-pinned external actions; and measure API points, plan/apply latency, drift age, failed applies and rollback time before scaling. [uncertain]
recommended_design: Adopt a two-layer configuration system. Layer A is a vendor-neutral, versioned `.agent-os/config.yaml` validated against a pinned JSON Schema. Layer B is a deterministic GitHub adapter/controller that compiles the manifest into repository files plus remote intents. The checked-in manifest is desired intent; the controller database/event log and GitHub are operational state. Never derive approval from agent prose.

Distribute a small consumer surface: thin local caller workflows and repository instructions stay reviewable in each repo; complex verified jobs live in `ORG/agent-os-distribution`; the controller/CLI ships as a signed container and release artifact. Consumers pin reusable workflows/actions by full commit SHA, record the friendly bundle release and artifact digest in `.agent-os/distribution.lock`, and let Renovate or the controller propose—not merge—upgrade PRs [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use; https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/github-actions/].

Use a GitHub App, not a broad PAT. Separate installations/roles: `repo-bootstrap` can read metadata and create content PRs; `project-reconciler` has organization Projects read/write but no code write; `ruleset-reconciler` has the necessary administration capability and is invoked only after exact-plan human approval; worker workflows get explicit job-level `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions, normally `contents: read` and nothing else [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/authenticate-with-github_token; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions].

Represent Project field/status names symbolically in Git, but discover remote node IDs/options every reconciliation. Calculate canonical desired and observed hashes. Preview create/update/adopt/prune operations. By default create missing safe objects and report all conflicting/extra objects; never auto-delete a field, option, item or ruleset. An approved apply binds repository/project, plan hash, desired commit, policy/bundle versions, expiry and actor.

Keep self-improvement one-way: telemetry may open a change proposal under `evals/proposals/`; an independent evaluator runs protected cases; a human policy owner approves the exact commit/digest; canary repositories receive it; rollback restores the last lock. An agent that authored a prompt, evaluator, workflow, schema, permission or ruleset change cannot approve or promote it.
state_and_event_contract: Desired record: `{apiVersion, kind, metadata{name, owners, schemaVersion}, spec{repository, project, states, transitions, riskTiers, capabilities, workflows, gates, reconciliation, distribution}}`. Required identifiers are symbolic and stable (`stateKey`, `fieldKey`, `workflowKey`); display names are mutable attributes. `schemaVersion` selects validation/migration rules; `distribution.lock` binds release tag, Git commit SHA, OCI digest, schema digest and generated-file hashes.

Observed snapshot: `{scope, fetchedAt, sourceVersions, repositories[], project{id, number, fields[{id,key/name,type,options[]}], items[{id,contentId,fieldValues}]}, rulesets[], actionsPolicy, customProperties, localHeadSha, observedHash}`. Remote IDs never enter the portable desired manifest. Discovery fails closed on duplicate/ambiguous names unless an explicit, reviewed mapping is stored in the controller's encrypted state.

Plan/apply event: `{eventId, deliveryId, correlationId, controllerVersion, desiredCommit, desiredHash, observedHashBefore, operations[{op,resource,remoteId?,beforeHash?,after}], risk, approvers[], approvalHash?, attempt, outcome, observedHashAfter, timestamps}`. Idempotency key is `scope + desiredHash + observedHashBefore + operation-set hash`; webhook `X-GitHub-Delivery` is separately deduplicated. Store append-only audit events and an outbox before external effects.

Reconciliation loop: webhook or schedule -> authenticate/authorize -> inventory all relevant pages -> canonicalize -> diff -> classify. `report` emits drift only; `adopt` creates a PR updating allowed desired attributes; `enforce` applies safe non-destructive drift; `prune` is off unless an exact destructive plan is human-approved. Serialize one writer per project/ruleset scope. Because Project mutations do not offer a documented cross-call transaction or compare-and-swap, re-read immediately before risky writes, stop if `observedHash` changed, apply one idempotent operation, then re-read and record the result [separate add/update calls: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects].

State changes for work items remain control-plane events. A reconciler may project a committed `READY` state into a Project single-select field only after checking an approval token bound to `{workItemId,specHash,policyVersion,expiry}`. A manual Project edit is detected as drift and either reverted (strict managed field), adopted by reviewed PR (adoptable metadata), or quarantined (ambiguous); it never silently rewrites the durable workflow ledger.
repository_artifacts: Required consumer layout: `AGENTS.md`; `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (short generated/vendor adapter, not a second policy source); `.github/instructions/security.instructions.md`; `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml`, `bug.yml`, `config.yml`; `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; `.github/CODEOWNERS`; `.github/workflows/agent-policy.yml`, `agent-verify.yml`, `agent-reconcile-plan.yml` (thin pinned callers); `.agent-os/config.yaml`; `.agent-os/distribution.lock`; `.agent-os/schemas/config.schema.json`, `work-item.schema.json`, `event.schema.json`, `evidence.schema.json`; `.agent-os/migrations/`; `policy/rego/`; `evals/cases/`, `evals/manifest.yaml`, `evals/proposals/`; `runbooks/reconcile.md`, `upgrade.md`, `rollback.md`, `break-glass.md`.

Exact top-level schema: `apiVersion: agent-os.dev/v1alpha1`; `kind: RepositoryAgentPolicy`; `metadata: {name, owners[], schemaVersion}`; `spec.repository: {provider, owner, name, defaultBranch, customPropertySelector}`; `spec.project: {owner, number, managedFields[], unmanagedFields[], driftMode}`; `spec.states[]: {key, displayName, terminal, projectOption}`; `spec.transitions[]: {from, to, event, guard, approvalClass}`; `spec.riskTiers[]`; `spec.capabilityProfiles[]: {id, paths, tokenPermissions, egress, secrets, ttl, budget}`; `spec.workflows[]: {key, reusableRef, inputs, requiredChecks}`; `spec.gates[]: {resourcePatterns, approverRoles, minApprovals, bind[]}`; `spec.reconciliation: {interval, safeCreate, enforce[], adopt[], prune:false}`; `spec.distribution: {channel, compatibility, lockRequired}`. JSON Schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, required arrays/keys, enumerations and URI/hash patterns [JSON Schema core: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core].

Central distribution repository layout: `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, `reconcile-plan.yml`, `eval.yml`; `actions/setup/action.yml`, `actions/collect-evidence/action.yml`; `workflow-templates/agent-os.yml` and `agent-os.properties.json`; `schemas/v1alpha1/*.json`; `migrations/<from>-to-<to>/`; `cmd/agent-os`; `adapters/github/`; `policy/`; `test/fixtures/repos/`; `compatibility.yaml`; `CHANGELOG.md`; release provenance/SBOM. Workflow templates follow GitHub's exact paired-file convention [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/create-workflow-templates].

CODEOWNERS must cover `/.agent-os/`, `/.github/workflows/`, `/.github/CODEOWNERS`, `/policy/`, `/evals/`, `/AGENTS.md`, and the lock file, while rulesets require the named check and code-owner reviews. CODEOWNERS is only effective as a gate when branch/ruleset policy requires review; the file alone merely requests owners [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners].
workflow_steps: Bootstrap: an owner creates the custom-property schema and sets `agent-os=pilot` on opted-in repositories; the App inventories selected repos; render deterministic local files; open a PR with config, lock, owners, exact permissions and a remote-change preview. Do not apply rulesets/Project writes before the repo owners approve the PR and the controller verifies the merged commit. Custom properties are the inventory selector, not authorization [https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-custom-properties-for-repositories-in-your-organization].

Validate PR: verify JSON Schema and cross-field invariants; reject unknown keys; render twice and compare; run actionlint/yamllint, zizmor, OPA tests, secret scan and CODEOWNERS coverage; ensure every `uses:` outside the repository is a full SHA; calculate proposed capabilities against current capabilities; produce a signed plan artifact. Stop on schema ambiguity, privilege increase, mutable reference, missing owner, unsafe event/context, or modified protected eval/oracle.

Merge and reconcile: after current-head checks and required human approval, merge the repository-files PR. Controller receives the push/webhook, verifies HMAC and installation/repo identity, deduplicates delivery, reads the merged SHA, inventories GitHub, produces a fresh plan, and auto-applies only allowlisted creates/updates with no capability expansion. A ruleset, permission, Project field deletion/rename, state semantic change or bypass change waits for an exact-plan approval. Re-read after every external write; on drift, abort and replan.

Upgrade: release central bundle with changelog, compatibility matrix, SBOM/provenance and immutable SHA/digest; discover consumers from audit/API or lock files; open one upgrade PR per cohort updating pin, lock, generated files and required migration; run N and N-1 contract/eval suites; canary 1-2 repositories; observe a declared window; then widen. Stop on any policy invariant regression, elevated permission, unresolved manual edit, API preview break, or rollback test failure. Template repositories are used only for day-zero creation, never fleet upgrades [https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-repository-from-a-template].

Rollback: disable the new controller release, restore the prior immutable workflow SHA/OCI digest in a PR, switch the affected reconciler to `report`, cancel queued applies, and reconcile forward from a fresh inventory. Do not attempt `git revert` as if it atomically undid already-applied Project/ruleset mutations; execute recorded compensating operations only where tested and require a human for destructive restoration.
human_gates: Repository owners approve the first bootstrap PR and the exact generated diff. A platform/security owner separately approves the first remote apply and any GitHub App permission set. Approval binds repo/project, desired commit/hash, plan hash, distribution/schema/policy versions and expiry; any new commit or changed observed hash invalidates it.

Mandatory human gate: workflow/action code, `pull_request_target`, token permission, secret/egress/runner, GitHub App, CODEOWNERS, ruleset/bypass, state semantics, protected acceptance tests/evals, evaluator or migration change; Project deletion/field-option removal/rename; adoption of manual drift; major schema/bundle upgrade; exception or break-glass. At least two roles approve critical permission/policy changes where feasible.

Agents may draft config, migration and evaluation proposals and explain a plan. They cannot approve a change they authored, change the required approver set, mark their own eval as sufficient, grant a new capability, delete audit evidence, or promote/canary themselves. Protected rulesets and separate credentials enforce this rather than an instruction file.
security_and_failure_modes: Supply-chain compromise or moved tags: pin every third-party action and reusable workflow to a reviewed full SHA, verify provenance/repository origin, restrict allowed actions, scan with Scorecard/zizmor, and update by reviewed PR. The `tj-actions/changed-files` incident shows tags were retroactively repointed and secrets printed [https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised].

Privilege confused deputy: called workflows cannot elevate the caller token, but an overly broad caller still passes broad authority. Set `permissions: {}` at workflow root and explicit minimum job scopes; pass named secrets rather than `secrets: inherit`; separate Projects/rulesets App identities; never check out or execute untrusted PR code in a privileged `pull_request_target` job [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use].

Prompt/config injection: issue bodies, repository text, generated output and PR metadata are untrusted. Parse schemas, escape shell arguments via environment/input APIs, allowlist operations and egress, and authorize every tool call outside the model. `AGENTS.md` improves context but cannot confer permission [AgentDojo: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352].

Remote drift/races: renamed/duplicate Project fields, concurrent human edits, stale node IDs, partial GraphQL success, reordered/duplicate/missed webhooks, rate limits and secondary throttling. Mitigate with stable symbolic keys plus rediscovery, one-writer leases, canonical hashes, pre/post inventory, per-operation journal/outbox, bounded exponential backoff with jitter, dead-letter queue, scheduled full scans and non-destructive default [Projects webhooks preview: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects-v2; API limits: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api].

Fleet blast radius: a bad central workflow or migration affects every consumer. Pin releases, phase cohorts, cap concurrency, install kill switches, run canaries, retain N-1, and require local thin callers so each repository can freeze. Private sharing can leak logs to outside collaborators, so never embed proprietary source/policy in runtime output [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/share-across-private-repositories].

Git/remote split brain: merging desired configuration does not mean GitHub accepted or retained it. Report `DesiredCommitted`, `ApplyPending`, `AppliedVerified`, `Drifted`, `Blocked`, or `RollbackRequired`; never display `Applied` before post-read equality. A failed compensator escalates, preserves evidence and leaves reconciliation in report-only mode.
validation_and_tests: Schema/unit: validate valid/invalid fixtures against pinned Draft 2020-12 schemas; property-test duplicate keys, cycles, illegal transitions and capability escalation; snapshot canonical rendering; assert `additionalProperties:false`; test every migration for forward conversion, idempotence and (when promised) reverse conversion [https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core].

Workflow/security: actionlint/yamllint; zizmor and OpenSSF Scorecard pin checks; search all `uses:` refs for 40-hex SHA policy; test expression/shell injection fixtures; assert exact `permissions`; verify fork PRs cannot reach secrets/write tokens; enforce CODEOWNERS/rulesets in an ephemeral repository. ARGUS evidence justifies taint-oriented tests, not only YAML syntax checks [https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity23/presentation/muralee].

Controller contract: recorded GraphQL/REST fixtures plus a disposable organization/project test. Exercise pagination, REDACTED Project items, stale/renamed IDs, separate add/update calls, partial errors, 403/404/409/422/429/5xx, rate resets, webhook replay/reorder/omission, crash after remote success before journal commit, lease expiry and outbox replay. Assert at-most-one intended effect under at-least-once attempts and that deletes never occur without a valid bound approval.

Drift/upgrade: golden desired-observed-plan cases for create, update, manual edit, ambiguous duplicate, adopt and prune; canary live API probes for all used schema fields/mutations; N/N-1 consumer matrix; rollback rehearsal after partial Project/ruleset apply; cohort failure halts rollout. Compare post-read normalized remote state and required GitHub rules, not only a green Action.

Governance/eval: protected negative cases prove an author cannot approve itself, weaken tests, expand permissions, rewrite the baseline, or promote after a composite score hides a safety regression. Independent verifier signs the result for the exact commit and bundle digest; policy promotion requires invariant-by-invariant pass plus named human approval.
operational_maintenance: Run webhook-triggered incremental reconciliation plus scheduled full inventory. Dashboards: desired commit, installed bundle/schema, last observed/applied hashes, drift class/age, queue lag, API points/throttles, apply/rollback failures, stale locks, repositories off supported versions, mutable refs, unowned policy files and expiring exceptions. Projects preview changes and GraphQL deprecations enter a compatibility watch [https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects-v2].

Version three things independently: schema (`schemaVersion`, SemVer after stable v1), distribution bundle (SemVer release and immutable Git SHA/OCI digest), and repository policy revision (Git commit/content hash). Maintain a compatibility matrix and at least N/N-1; breaking schema or removed capability is a major release, additive optional field a minor, defect-only renderer change a patch [https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html]. Pre-1.0 `v1alpha1` changes still require explicit migrations and changelog.

Runbooks cover reconcile blockage, API preview/schema change, revoked App installation, rate exhaustion, ambiguous field, compromised action, leaked log/secret rotation, failed migration, partial apply, rollback and break-glass. Quarterly: minimize GitHub App permissions, audit bypass actors and Actions allowlists, test restore/kill switch, prune expired approvals/exceptions, rotate credentials, verify release provenance and sample repositories for local divergence.

For decommissioning, switch to report-only, export an observed snapshot/audit log, remove managed markers, revoke App installation, and use a human-approved cleanup plan. Preserve work-item/event/evidence records per retention policy; never silently delete Project fields/items merely because a repository was archived.
maturity_and_uncertainty: Solved/mature: repository files, issue forms, CODEOWNERS, GitHub Actions, reusable workflows/composite actions, immutable SHA pins, template repositories, JSON Schema, SemVer and GitHub App installations are established mechanisms with direct documentation.

Conditional: fleet bootstrap, policy compilation, remote ruleset reconciliation and non-destructive Project field projection are implementable but require a custom controller, repository-specific permissions, live API contract tests, drift ownership and staged rollout. GitHub supplies APIs, not a complete GitOps reconciler.

Experimental/unstable: treating Projects v2 webhooks as the sole state feed is unjustified because current GitHub docs call them public preview; Project coverage for every UI surface and atomic compare-and-swap behavior is not established. implementation_recommendation: Phase 0 (one week): freeze the v1alpha1 schema and directory contract; write JSON Schemas, renderer, config linter, `distribution.lock`, threat model and golden fixtures; create the central reusable `verify.yml`; pin all dependencies; protect policy/workflow/eval paths. Do not write Projects/rulesets yet.

Phase 1 (2-4 weeks, 2 repositories): GitHub App opens bootstrap PRs selected by `agent-os=pilot`; thin workflows call an immutable central SHA; CI emits signed plan/evidence; controller inventories one organization Project and reports normalized drift only. Establish API budgets, manual ownership and rollback baseline.

Phase 2 (4-8 weeks, <=10 repositories): enable safe create/update for allowlisted Project fields/options and a named ruleset after exact-plan approval; add scheduled inventory, outbox/idempotency, live sandbox contract tests, cohort upgrade PRs, N-1 rollback and dashboards. Keep prune/deletion off and human edits quarantined.

Phase 3: allow automatic correction only for locally proven low-risk drift, with per-repo freeze, capped concurrency and audit sampling. Centralize organization rules where this reduces duplication, but keep repository manifests as explicit overlays. Self-improvement remains proposal/eval/human-promotion. Do not adopt floating `@main`, `secrets: inherit`, autonomous ruleset/permission changes, template-based fleet upgrades, or Project-as-the-only-source-of-truth.

conflicts: Git looks like 'status as code', but GitHub Projects state lives in a mutable SaaS data model addressed by GraphQL node IDs. Resolution: Git stores desired mappings/policy and immutable approval/evidence references; the controller ledger owns transitions; GitHub Project fields are a reconciled projection. Webhooks speed detection but preview status and delivery realities require full polling [https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-api-to-manage-projects; https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#projects-v2].

Reusable workflows promise central updates, while immutable security requires consumers to pin a commit. Floating tags improve propagation but can be moved, as the `tj-actions` attack demonstrated. Resolution: pin SHA/digest, use discovery plus automated upgrade PRs and cohorts; accept controlled rollout latency instead of ambient trust [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use; https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised].

Organization defaults/templates reduce duplication, but local files override default health files and repositories created from templates do not inherit future changes. Resolution: defaults are fallbacks and templates are day-zero scaffolds; a versioned bundle plus lock/reconciler is the upgrade system [https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file; https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-repository-from-a-template].

Central private workflows appear to protect intellectual property, but GitHub warns consuming-repository outside collaborators can indirectly access the private repo and view logs. Resolution: minimize shared code/output, isolate secrets, restrict consumer access and use public/non-secret policy where possible [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/share-across-private-repositories].
